name: manual_4a07d7
claim: LAN peer direct drops (lan_peer_assign.py drop) leave NO outbox sidecar, so a 'no-record' state after a send is normal, not a failure. Success evidence is the drop's own JSON (ok true with received_at and bytes). Run the send helper once per file and capture its full output to a file instead of tailing it, because a truncated tail hid the result and a rerun would duplicate the file (an 8,642-byte file was sent twice this way).
conditions: lan_peer drop outbox sidecar no-record duplicate send

decisions.notes: Observed 2026-11-10 across three sends; the receipt table from the peer later confirmed byte counts.

rationale: Observed 2026-11-10 across three sends; the receipt table from the peer later confirmed byte counts.
